title: Half of this map's people live in 5 of its 42 countries.
source: Source: World Bank Open Data, indicator SP.POP.TOTL (population, total), 2023
dotKey: 1 dot = 199,000 people — 2,996 dots drawn for 596,770,599 people
meterCaption: Share of this map's population drawn
conclusion: Germany, United Kingdom, France, Italy and Spain hold 327,522,303 of 596,770,599 people — 54.9%. The first four hold 46.8%.
caveat: Each country gets the SAME slice of the clock, so time on screen is not population — the meter is. A dot's position inside its country is random, so a cluster edge is not a settlement, and a tighter fill means more people per square kilometre than a bigger population. Russia and seven micro-territories with no independent World Bank figure are excluded.
alt: Map of Europe filling with dots, one dot per 199,000 people, 2,996 dots in all. Every one of the 42 countries is outlined and empty before the sequence starts, then they fill in largest first, each taking the same slice of time, while a bar under the map reads the share of the map's population drawn. The bar passes its half-way mark at the fiveth country of 42: Germany, United Kingdom, France, Italy and Spain together hold 327,522,303 of 596,770,599 people, 54.9%, against 46.8% for the first four. The remaining 37 countries take seven eighths of the sequence to add the rest, and the last to arrive, Liechtenstein, holds 39,846 people.
